([[Hillside, New Jersey]]) | career_start = 2021 | career_end = | years1 = 2021–present | team1 = [[NBA G League Ignite]] | highlights = }} '''Jonathan Malangu Kuminga''' (born 6 October 2002) is a Congolese professional [[basketball]] player for the [[NBA G League Ignite]] of the [[NBA G League]]. Listed at {{convert|6|ft|6|in|m|2}} and {{convert|210|lbs|kg|0}}, he plays the [[small forward]] and [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] positions. A consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and the top [[Small forward|small forward]] in the 2021 class, he chose to forgo his [[college basketball|college]] eligibility and reclassify to the 2020 class to join the Ignite. Kuminga finished his high school career at [[St. Patrick High School (New Jersey)|The Patrick School]] in [[Hillside, New Jersey]]. ==Early life== Kuminga began playing basketball in the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] at the age of two.{{cite web |url=https://www.zagsblog.com/2019/07/13/jonathan-kuminga-makes-case-for-no-1-high-school-player-in-the-nation-talks-future-plans/ |title=Jonathan Kuminga makes case for No. 1 high school player in the nation, talks future plans |first=Adam |last=Zagoria |work=ZagsBlog |date=13 July 2019 |access-date=11 August 2019}} In 2016, he moved to the United States to play high school basketball.{{cite web |last1=Jordan |first1=Jason |title=SI All-American TV: Top 2021 F Jonathan Kuminga Speaks on Social Injustice In Democratic Republic of Congo |url=https://www.si.com/college/recruiting/basketball/jonathan-kuminga-social-injustice-2021-duke-kentucky-auburn-texas-tech |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=16 July 2020 |date=7 July 2020}} ==High school career== As a freshman, Kuminga played basketball for [[Huntington Prep School]] in [[Huntington, West Virginia]].{{cite web |last1=Burlison |first1=Frank |title=Two elite 2022 guards among Pangos East standouts |url=http://www.burlisononbasketball.com/2018/10/two-elite-2022-guards-among-pangos-east-standouts/ |publisher=Burlison on Basketball |access-date=14 August 2019 |date=28 October 2018}} For his sophomore season, he transferred to Our Savior New American School in [[Centereach, New York]] and averaged 25 points, five rebounds, and five assists per game.{{cite web |last1=Divens |first1=Jordan |title=2018-19 MaxPreps Boys Basketball Sophomore All-American Team |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/wCRc7AkDlUOzrgbdS9nvZA/2018-19-maxpreps-boys-basketball-sophomore-all-american-team.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=14 August 2019 |date=18 April 2019}} In January 2019, Kuminga was named [[most valuable player]] of the Slam Dunk to the Beach showcase after scoring 40 points, a single-game record at the event, in a loss to [[Gonzaga College High School]].{{cite web |last1=Riedel |first1=Kenny |title=Slam Dunk superlatives |url=https://www.capegazette.com/article/slam-dunk-superlatives/172369 |website=[[Cape Gazette]] |access-date=14 August 2019 |date=2 January 2019}} He earned [[MaxPreps National Basketball Player of the Year awards#Sophomore of the Year|MaxPreps National Sophomore of the Year]] honors. After the season, Kuminga averaged 20.8 points, 5.2 rebounds and 3.3 assists per game for the NY Rens at the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League]], facing many players older than him. He scored 43 points, shooting 7-of-11 from three-point range, against the Texas Titans, a team featuring top recruits [[Cade Cunningham]] and [[Greg Brown (basketball, born 2001)|Greg Brown]].{{cite web |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-recruiting/article231895998.html |title=UK basketball scholarship offer led to (very) long-distance phone call for top recruit |first=Ben |last=Roberts |work=Kentucky.com |date=25 June 2019 |access-date=11 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190629055013/https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-recruiting/article231895998.html |archive-date=29 June 2019 |url-status=live}} For his junior season, Kuminga transferred to [[The Patrick School]] in [[Hillside, New Jersey]].{{cite web |last1=Jordan |first1=Jason |title=No. 1 Chosen 25 junior Jonathan Kuminga transfers to The Patrick School |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2019/jonathan-kuminga-transfers-to-the-patrick-school |publisher=USA Today High School Sports |access-date=19 May 2020 |date=26 August 2017}} On 23 December 2019, he made his season debut, scoring 20 points in a win over [[Roselle Catholic High School]], after having been ruled ineligible for 30 days by the [[New Jersey State Interscholastic Athletic Association]] due to transfer rules.{{cite web |last1=Zagoria |first1=Adam |title=Jonathan Kuminga scores 20 in Patrick School debut after judge grants stay |url=https://www.zagsblog.com/2019/12/23/jonathan-kuminga-is-now-immediately-eligible-at-the-patrick-school-after-judge-grants-stay/ |publisher=Zagsblog |access-date=19 May 2020 |date=23 December 2019}} On 3 January 2020, Kuminga suffered an ankle sprain that sidelined him for about one month.{{cite web |last1=Corrigan |first1=James |title=Jonathan Kuminga returns from ankle injury, discusses Kobe's impact on his life |url=https://www.zagsblog.com/2020/02/05/jonathan-kuminga-returns-from-ankle-injury-discusses-kobes-impact-on-his-life/ |publisher=Zagsblog |access-date=19 May 2020 |date=5 February 2020}} As a junior, he averaged 16.2 points, 5.5 rebounds and 3.7 assists per game.{{cite web |last1=Greco |first1=Richard |last2=Kinney |first2=Mike |last3=Minnick |first3=Kevin |title=Boys Basketball: Second team All-State, 2019-2020 |url=https://www.nj.com/highschoolsports/2020/03/boys-basketball-second-team-all-state-2019-2020.html |publisher=[[NJ.com]] |access-date=19 May 2020 |date=25 March 2020}} ===Recruiting=== As a high school sophomore, Kuminga emerged as one of the best [[college recruiting|recruits]] in the 2021 class, with most recruiting services ranking him number one in his class by the time he was a junior.{{cite web |url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/Hoophall-Jonathan-Kuminga-shows-progression-as-high-majors-pursue-128074717/ |title=Hoophall: Jonathan Kuminga progresses, as high majors pursue |first=Evan |last=Daniels |work=[[247Sports.com]] |date=20 January 2019 |access-date=11 August 2019}} On 15 July 2020, he reclassified to the 2020 class and announced that he would bypass [[college basketball]] to join the [[NBA G League Ignite]] over offers from [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech]], [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] and [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], among other college programs.{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Top-five prospect Jonathan Kuminga latest to bypass college for G League |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29470941/top-five-prospect-jonathan-kuminga-latest-bypass-college-g-league |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=16 July 2020 |date=15 July 2020}} At the end of his high school career, he was a consensus five-star recruit and the best [[small forward]] in the 2020 class. He was considered the third-best player in his class by [[Rivals.com]] and the fourth-best by [[247Sports.com]] and [[ESPN]] after reclassifying .{{cite web |title=Jonathan Kuminga, 2020 Small forward |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2021/jonathan-kuminga-208382 |publisher=[[Rivals.com]] |access-date=16 July 2020}}{{cite web |title=Jonathan Kuminga - Basketball Recruiting - Player Ignite]], a developmental team affiliated with the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web |title=Five-Star Recruit Jonathan Kuminga Signs With NBA G League |url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/five-star-recruit-jonathan-kuminga-signs-with-nba-g-league/ |publisher=[[NBA G League]] |access-date=16 July 2020 |date=16 July 2020}} On 10 February 2021, he made his debut, recording 19 points, four assists and four rebounds in a 110–104 win over the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]].{{cite web |last1=Irving |first1=Kyle |title=Jonathan Kuminga and Jalen Green: How did 2021 NBA Draft prospects play in their G League Ignite debut? |url=https://ca.nba.com/news/jonathan-kuminga-jalen-green-how-did-2021-nba-draft-prospects-play-in-their-g-league-ignite-debut-santa-cruz-warriors/12b0us3movepa13j1js64rb178 |publisher=[[National Basketball Association]] |access-date=23 April 2021 |date=11 February 2021}} Kuminga averaged 15.8 points, 7.2 rebounds and 2.7 assists per game.{{cite web |last1=Irving |first1=Kyle |title=2021 NBA |url=https://ca.nba.com/news/2021-nba-draft-jonathan-kuminga-g-league-ignite-scouting-report-strengths-weaknesses-and-player-comparisons-/11dsklbxfsdaw1v9u31g1umb4t |publisher=[[National Basketball
